previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, kidney transplantation, and breast cancer was admitted for fever, congestion, and an abnormal urinalysis. She had a two-month history of URI-like symptoms with recent worsening and a temperature of 101.7°F. Empiric IV cefepime was started in the ED, and she was admitted for monitoring. Workup revealed no pneumonia on chest X-ray and a normal transplant kidney ultrasound except for mildly increased resistive indices. Urine culture grew E. coli sensitive to cefpodoxime, and she was transitioned to oral therapy. She remained afebrile, and symptoms improved. Discharge included a 13-day course of cefpodoxime, continuation of all home medications including cyclosporine and atorvastatin, and nasal sprays for sinus symptoms. Medication adherence, especially for cilostazol and cyclosporine, was emphasized. Follow-up appointments were advanced.
